To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the superconducting transition of YBCO single crystals is fully anisotropic when the magnetic field is tilted from the c-axis.

the fully anisotropic superconductor YBa2Cu 3O 7-δ exhibits a first-order vortex solid-to- liquid transition in a tilted magnetic field, and the transition temperature Tc, which is a measure of the vortex liquid phase, depends on the angle θ of the tilted magnetic field.
The superconducting vortex lattice undergoes a fully anisotropic superconductor-to-insulator transition when a tilted magnetic field is applied to an ion irradiated YBCO single crystal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the superconducting transition of heavy ion irradiated untwinned high-temperature superconducting single crystals YBa2Cu2O7-delta.
the superconducting properties of ion-irradiation YBCO single crystal samples with the magnetic field direction tilted from the c-axis.
the development of a new type of superconductor, the heavy-ion-irradiated high-Tc cuprate, which has the potential to be used in the construction of a high-temperature superconducting magnet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fully anisotropic vortex-solid to vortex-liquid transition in ion irradiation induced anisotropic YBa2Cu307-delta single crystals is fully consistent with the predictions of the two-fluid model of superconductivity, where the superconducting condensate is treated as a normal Fermi gas with the Fermi energy EF and Fermi temperature TF, and the superfluid density ns is given by the BCS relation ns=(2m*/h2)kBTcF.

the superconducting properties of YBa2Cu 3O 7-δ single crystals irradiated with heavy ions (Ar, Au) are not affected by the presence of point defects and the formation of disordered regions, but by the formation of dislocations.
the fully anisotropic superconductor YBa2Cu307-delta undergoes an anisotropic super-conducting transition when irradiated by heavy ions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vortex liquid phase in YBCO can be stabilized by irradiation and that the superconducting transition becomes fully anisotropic in the case of tilted field.
the anisotropy of the superconducting transition temperature in YBCO is a consequence of the anisotropies in the electronic structure and the electron-phonon coupling.
we have shown that the vortex solid-liquid phase transition is fully anisotropic in YBa2Cu307-delta.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vortex liquid phase in the high field region is fully anisotropic and the vortex liquid phase is not isotropic as was previously assumed.
the vortex liquid state in ion irradiated samples has an anisotropy that is very close to that of the normal state.

the vortex liquid-solid transition in YBCO is fully anisotropic and the transition temperature Tc is strongly dependent on the angle between the field and the CuO2 plane, with Tc increasing by 20% as the field is tilted from the CuO2 planes to the ab plane.
